5525cff600f31aa4.title: Maxone Plus Soft Capsule
5525cff600f31aa4.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E and B1 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, and in old age; to relieve peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.); and for beriberi, eye fatigue, and muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency.
5525cff600f31aa4.usage:
Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
5525cff600f31aa4.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 12 months of age; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or conditions requiring careful use of lipid emulsions; conditions at particular risk from fat overload; a predisposition to thrombosis.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins E and B1 and relieves peripheral circulatory disturbance, menopausal symptoms, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, and muscle cramps caused by magnesium deficiency
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, recovery, and old age, shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness and coldness of hands and feet, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, beriberi, eye fatigue, muscle cramps

5ce4a14458a28973.usage:
Adolescents aged 12 years and older and adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 2 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
5ce4a14458a28973.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 12 months of age; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: premature infants, infants; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or conditions requiring careful use of lipid emulsions; conditions at particular risk from fat overload; a predisposition to thrombosis (blocked blood vessels); hypersensitivity or past hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

While taking this medicine, do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen, anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or intravenous lipid preparations. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

5e57d1b6c389c411.title: 2XB Gold 100 Tablet
5e57d1b6c389c411.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E, B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age; to relieve beriberi, eye fatigue, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (lower back pain, shoulder stiffness, etc.), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
5e57d1b6c389c411.usage:
Adults and children aged 8 years and older: take 1 tablet, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
5e57d1b6c389c411.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: hyperoxaluria; premature infants, infants; gastrointestinal disorders such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional colitis; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; gout; kidney stones.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. This medicine may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values, or interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with anti-aldosterone agents, triamterene, or oral contraceptives containing estrogen. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, constipation, stomach discomfort, gastrointestinal disturbance, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, rash, redness, red spots, asystole (cardiac arrest), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, odor in sweat or breath, hair loss, restlessness, low blood pressure, pulmonary edema, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins E, B1, B2, B6, C and zinc, and relieves beriberi, eye fatigue, neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, and oral and skin inflammation
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, recovery, growth periods, and old age, beriberi, eye fatigue, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, zinc supply

6dcb3dfa6dad92ad.title: Benforex Capsule
6dcb3dfa6dad92ad.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins when demand increases and dietary intake is insufficient (wasting diseases, pregnant women, breastfeeding women), and for neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, peripheral neuritis (alcoholic, diabetic), and peripheral nerve paralysis where deficiency or metabolic disturbance of the vitamins contained in this product is suspected.
6dcb3dfa6dad92ad.usage:
Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 1 to 2 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
6dcb3dfa6dad92ad.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hereditary conditions such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian.

Consult a pharmacist before taking together with levodopa.

If hypersensitivity reactions such as rash or itching occur, though rare, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist. Loss of appetite, stomach (upper abdominal) discomfort, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea may occasionally occur.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins when demand increases, and helps with neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, peripheral neuritis, and peripheral nerve paralysis where vitamin deficiency or metabolic disturbance is suspected
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Vitamin supply for wasting diseases, pregnant and breastfeeding women, neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain, peripheral neuritis (alcoholic, diabetic), peripheral nerve paralysis

82324f96e58e3466.title: Lovital Soft Capsule
82324f96e58e3466.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E, B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, and in old age, and to relieve peripheral circulatory disturbance and menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of the hands and feet, and cold hands and feet.
82324f96e58e3466.usage:
Adults and children aged 8 years and older: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
82324f96e58e3466.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine or to soybean oil, soybeans, or peanuts; infants under 3 months of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: infants under 1 year of age; premature infants, infants; hyperoxaluria (excess oxalate excreted in the urine); disorders of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinemia, diabetic hyperlipidemia, or pancreatitis, or conditions requiring careful use of lipid emulsions; conditions at particular risk from fat overload; a predisposition to thrombosis (blocked blood vessels); folic acid deficiency; hypersensitivity or past hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may interfere with the detection of glucose in various urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting laboratory test values. When giving to children, administer under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before using together with oral contraceptives containing estrogen or intravenous lipid preparations.

If stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, menstruation starting earlier than expected, gradually heavier menstrual flow, or prolonged bleeding occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, recovery, and old age, shoulder and neck stiffness, numbness of hands and feet, cold hands and feet

838accb04dda5160.title: Trigel Tablet
838accb04dda5160.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, indigestion from overeating, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, and sour belching.
838accb04dda5160.usage:
Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, 3 times daily, swallowing quickly.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
838accb04dda5160.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; receiving dialysis; hypermagnesemia; hyperphosphatemia; constipation; intestinal stenosis (narrowing); acute appendicitis; women within the first 3 months of pregnancy; children under 7 years of age.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: past hypermagnesemia or magnesium deficiency; past kidney disorder or kidney disease.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

When taking, swallow quickly to avoid leaving a numb feeling in the mouth.

Do not take together with tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a pharmacist before using together with digoxin, captopril, cimetidine, ranitidine, famotidine, theophylline, propranolol, atenolol, ferrous sulfate, chlorpromazine, acetylsalicylic acid, naproxen, metoprolol, levodopa, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, ketodeoxycholic acid, sodium fluoride, isoniazid, enoxacin, norfloxacin, levothyroxine, coumarin derivatives, or iron. Avoid carbonated drinks before taking this medicine.

If diarrhea, constipation, abdominal bloating, skin rash, numbness, phosphate deficiency, or, rarely, headache, drowsiness, dizziness, weakness, or accumulation of aluminum in nerve and bone tissue occurs, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Neutralizes stomach acid to relieve various stomach symptoms caused by excess acid
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Excess stomach acid, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach bloating, indigestion from overeating, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, sour belching

86ea446f1ffff152.title: Mybical Tablet
86ea446f1ffff152.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins D and B1 during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, lowered physical strength during or after illness, growth periods, and in old age, and to prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets.
86ea446f1ffff152.usage:
Adults: take 1 tablet at a time, once daily.
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
86ea446f1ffff152.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypercalcemia (excess calcium in the blood); sarcoidosis (an inflammatory disease of unknown cause affecting the whole body); kidney disease; hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months of age; kidney stones; severe renal failure.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, are breastfeeding, or have any of the following: premature infants, infants; cardiac or circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinemia; taking cardiac glycosides; past kidney stones.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics, or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking together with anti-aldosterone agents or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea or black tea while taking this medicine and around the time of taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loose stools, constipation, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, or skin rash occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Supplies vitamins D and B1 and helps prevent poor development of bones and teeth and rickets
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Physical fatigue, vitamin supply during pregnancy, breastfeeding, illness, recovery, growth periods, and old age, poor development of bones and teeth, prevention of rickets

89b7e1fcd52566a1.title: Benfos Tablet
89b7e1fcd52566a1.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used for nervous system disorders caused by vitamin B1 and B6 deficiency.
89b7e1fcd52566a1.usage:

Keep to the stated dose and directions.
89b7e1fcd52566a1.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

If hives, rash, itching, loss of appetite, abdominal bloating, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, neurotoxicity, or, in newborns and infants, severe sedation, low blood pressure, or breathing problems (difficulty breathing, apnea) occur, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.How it works: Helps improve nervous system disorders caused by vitamin B1 and B6 deficiency
summaryTable.Main symptoms: Nervous system disorders caused by vitamin B1 and B6 deficiency
